exercises.prompt: In قَرَأَ الطَّالِبُ كِتَابَ التَّارِيخِ, why does كِتَابَ end in a single fatḥah without أَلْ or tanwīn?
choices: It is the direct object (accusative) AND the muḍāf of an iḍāfah
It is the subject of the verb
exercises.answer: It is the direct object (accusative) AND the muḍāf of an iḍāfah
exercises.explanation: كِتَابَ receives the action of قَرَأَ (so it is accusative, -a) and is annexed to التَّارِيخِ (so as muḍāf it drops أَلْ and tanwīn).

feedback.rule: A noun's case comes from its sentence role; iḍāfah strips أَلْ and tanwīn from the muḍāf.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence element in قَرَأَ الطَّالِبُ كِتَابَ التَّارِيخِ فِي المَكْتَبَةِ to its grammatical role.
exercises.explanation: Executing the 3-step Iʿrāb Routine identifies the verbal clause, its nuclear components, and its governing factors.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to form: 'The student read the book of history.'
exercises.explanation: V-S-O order places قَرَأَ first, followed by الطَّالِبُ (fāʿil) and the iḍāfah object كِتَابَ التَّارِيخِ.
